title: Image-Based Identification of Ophthalmic Lens Optical Characteristics Using Local Texture Descriptors: A Benchmark Study for Non-Destructive Optical Inspection
content: Despite substantial progress in optical imaging and computer vision, the image-based identification of ophthalmic lens characteristics, such as refractive index and anti-reflective coating type, remains largely unexplored. This work introduces this problem as a non-destructive optical inspection task, where lens-induced visual changes are treated as subtle micro-texture signatures produced by the interaction between the lens and a controlled visual target. Although these signatures are often imperceptible to the human eye, they can be quantified using local texture analysis. To establish a first experimental reference for this emerging application, we present a systematic benchmark of state-of-the-art local texture descriptors, with particular emphasis on Local Binary Pattern (LBP)-like methods, under unified evaluation protocols. The evaluation is conducted on two dedicated ophthalmic lens image datasets acquired under controlled conditions, using consistent visual targets designed to reveal lens-induced texture and color variations. This setting enables a rigorous assessment of whether handcrafted micro-texture descriptors can encode latent optical properties related to refractive index and coating type. The experimental results show that several modern LBP variants achieve competitive recognition performance, confirming the relevance of local micro-texture analysis for image-based ophthalmic lens characteristic identification. Beyond accuracy, the study analyzes dataset dependence, the effect of training-set size, performance stability, and the influence of enriched local encoding strategies and neighborhood sampling schemes. Overall, this work introduces an image-based benchmark framework for non-destructive ophthalmic lens inspection and provides practical guidelines for selecting local texture descriptors in lens characteristic identification systems.
